If you want to know how to get PR in Canada after study, the usual route is to complete an eligible Canadian programme, obtain a Post-Graduation Work Permit, gain qualifying work experience and apply through Canadian Experience Class, Express Entry, a Provincial Nominee Program or another suitable pathway.

Here’s the thing: a Canadian course does not give you PR. It gives you education, time and an opportunity to build a profile that may qualify for permanent residence.

Canada Study-to-PR Pathway at a Glance

Your situation

Pathway to check first

You have one year of eligible Canadian skilled work

Canadian Experience Class

You already have skilled foreign work experience

Federal Skilled Worker Program

Your study, job or work experience fits a provincial stream

Provincial Nominee Program

You have strong French-language ability

French-category Express Entry or provincial routes

You have an eligible Atlantic employer and job offer

You intend to settle in Quebec

Most international graduates follow these steps:

  1. Choose a PGWP-eligible programme.
  2. Apply for a PGWP, if eligible.
  3. Find work that matches an eligible NOC and TEER category.
  4. Gain the required skilled work experience.
  5. Take an approved English or French test.
  6. Create an Express Entry profile or apply through another pathway.
  7. Receive an Invitation to Apply or provincial nomination.
  8. Submit a complete permanent residence application.

Can International Students Get PR in Canada After Study?

Canadian education may add points to an Express Entry profile. An eligible Canadian post-secondary credential lasting one or two years may add 15 CRS points. A credential lasting three years or more may add 30 points. An eligible master’s, professional or doctoral credential may also qualify for 30 additional points.

A provincial nomination can add 600 CRS points. However, education points alone rarely decide the outcome. Language ability and skilled work experience can make a much larger difference.

Consider two students who complete the same two-year diploma.

One finds a TEER 1 job, keeps detailed employment records and completes 1,560 eligible work hours. The other accepts a job that does not qualify for Canadian Experience Class.

Their education looks similar. Their PR positions do not.

PGWP to PR in Canada

The Post-Graduation Work Permit often connects Canadian study with permanent residence. It allows eligible graduates to gain Canadian work experience after completing their studies.

Graduating from a Designated Learning Institution does not automatically make you eligible for a PGWP. The particular programme must also qualify. Check the official PGWP eligibility requirements before paying a tuition deposit.

PGWP language requirements

Most graduates applying under the current rules must submit an approved English or French language result.

Type of programme

Minimum language level

Bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral degree

CLB 7 or NCLC 7

Other university programme

CLB 7 or NCLC 7

College, polytechnic or non-university programme

CLB 5 or NCLC 5

Bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral graduates do not have a PGWP field-of-study requirement.

Many graduates of other university, college, polytechnic and non-university programmes must complete an eligible field of study if they applied for their study permit on or after 1 November 2024.

IRCC has frozen the eligible field-of-study list for 2026. Check the exact Classification of Instructional Programs code for your programme rather than relying on its marketing title.

How long can a PGWP last?

Programme completed

Possible PGWP length

Eligible master’s programme lasting at least eight months

Up to three years

Other eligible programme lasting eight months to under two years

Usually up to the programme length

Eligible programme lasting two years or more

Up to three years

Two or more eligible programmes

Combined duration may be considered

Passport expiring early

Permit may be shortened

A mildly surprising point is that an eligible one-year master’s degree may lead to a longer PGWP than a one-year graduate certificate.

An eligible master’s programme lasting at least eight months may lead to a three-year PGWP, even when the programme lasted less than two years. For most other programmes shorter than two years, the permit may be issued for a period similar to the programme length.

Your passport expiry date can also shorten the permit. Renewing a passport before applying may prevent you from losing part of the period for which you could otherwise qualify.

The current PGWP government fee is CAD 255. This includes the CAD 155 work permit fee and the CAD 100 open work permit holder fee.

Canadian Experience Class After Study

Canadian Experience Class is one of the most practical pathways for graduates who gain skilled Canadian work experience.

Your work experience must generally:

  • fall within NOC TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3;
  • be paid;
  • be authorised;
  • be gained while you were physically working in Canada for a Canadian employer;
  • total at least one year or 1,560 hours;
  • have been gained during the three years before applying.

You can reach 1,560 hours through one full-time job, eligible part-time work or more than one qualifying job. IRCC counts no more than 30 hours per week towards the requirement.

IRCC assesses your actual duties, not only your job title. Your work should match the lead statement and most of the main duties for the NOC you claim.

Suppose your contract describes you as an operations manager, but your daily responsibilities match an administrative occupation. IRCC may assess the experience under the administrative NOC instead. The impressive title does not repair a duties mismatch.

Does student work count for CEC?

No. Work gained while you were a full-time student does not count towards the minimum Canadian work requirement for CEC, even when it was paid or completed during a co-op term.

Self-employment also does not normally count towards the CEC minimum, apart from a limited exception for certain physicians.

This is where many students calculate their timelines incorrectly. For CEC, the safer calculation normally begins when you start qualifying work after completing your studies and becoming authorised to work.

CEC eligibility does not mean immediate PR

Meeting the CEC requirements can make you eligible to enter the Express Entry pool. It does not allow you to submit a permanent residence application immediately.

IRCC ranks eligible candidates using CRS points. You must receive an Invitation to Apply before submitting your PR application.

Main PR Pathways After Study in Canada

Canadian Experience Class

CEC may suit you if you have at least one year of eligible Canadian skilled work and meet the language requirement.

You do not need a job offer or a separate educational qualification to meet the basic CEC requirements. Canadian education can still add CRS points and improve your profile.

For CEC, the minimum language level is generally:

Occupation

Minimum language level

TEER 0 or 1

CLB 7 or NCLC 7

TEER 2 or 3

CLB 5 or NCLC 5

A higher language result can add more CRS points, even after you meet the programme minimum.

Federal Skilled Worker Program

The Federal Skilled Worker Program may suit graduates who already have qualifying skilled work experience from outside Canada.

You generally need:

  • at least one year of continuous skilled work;
  • paid experience in TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3;
  • a minimum language level of CLB or NCLC 7;
  • at least 67 points under the FSWP selection grid;
  • an Educational Credential Assessment for eligible foreign education.

For example, a student with three years of foreign engineering experience may qualify for FSWP before completing one year of Canadian work.

Qualifying for FSWP does not guarantee an invitation. The applicant must still enter the Express Entry pool and achieve a competitive CRS score.

Provincial Nominee Program

A Provincial Nominee Program may help if your education, work experience, occupation or job offer matches a province’s needs.

Some provincial streams focus on:

  • graduates from institutions in that province;
  • applicants with local work experience;
  • workers in priority occupations;
  • candidates with eligible job offers;
  • French-speaking applicants.

An Express Entry-aligned provincial nomination adds 600 CRS points. You must genuinely intend to live in the province or territory that nominates you.

There is no universally easiest province for PR. A province becomes suitable when your profile matches an available stream.

Express Entry category-based selection

IRCC may hold Express Entry rounds for candidates with French-language ability or eligible experience in selected occupations.

The 2026 categories include healthcare and social services, STEM, trades, education, transport, certain physicians, researchers and senior managers with Canadian experience, as well as eligible skilled military recruits.

You must first qualify for a programme managed through Express Entry. Matching a category does not guarantee an invitation because candidates are still ranked within the relevant invitation round.

Valid job offers no longer receive the previous 50 or 200 CRS points. A job offer may still matter for employment, programme eligibility or a provincial pathway.

Quebec and regional pathways

Can I Apply for PR While Studying in Canada?

For example, a student with qualifying foreign skilled experience, an approved language result and a valid Educational Credential Assessment may qualify for FSWP while completing a Canadian degree.

However, full-time student work does not count towards the minimum Canadian work requirement for CEC.

How to Get PR in Canada After One-Year Study

PR after a one-year course is possible, but the timeframe may be tight.

A one-year non-master’s programme may lead to a PGWP of roughly the same length. If you spend four months finding qualifying employment, only eight months remain. That is normally not enough to complete the one-year CEC work requirement before the permit expires.

A one-year route may be more realistic when you already have:

  • skilled foreign work experience;
  • a strong language result;
  • a clear target occupation;
  • another possible pathway, such as FSWP or PNP.

The cheapest course is not always the safest plan. A short work permit can create much greater pressure after graduation.

How to Get PR in Canada After Two-Year Study

An eligible programme lasting two years or more may lead to a PGWP of up to three years.

That longer period can give you more time to:

  • find qualifying employment;
  • complete the CEC work requirement;
  • improve your language result;
  • build provincial connections;
  • wait for a suitable invitation round.

A two-year qualification still does not guarantee permanent residence. You must check the programme’s PGWP status, field-of-study requirement where applicable and connection with realistic skilled employment.

Students comparing study and career outcomes can explore programmes linked more closely with skilled work. Those managing a limited education budget may also compare lower-cost Canadian university options.

How to Get PR in Canada After a Master’s Degree

PR in Canada after a master’s degree may be possible through CEC, FSWP, PNP or category-based Express Entry.

An eligible master’s programme lasting at least eight months may lead to a three-year PGWP. Master’s graduates also avoid the PGWP field-of-study requirement, although they must still meet the language requirement.

Consider a graduate who completes a 12-month master’s degree, receives a three-year PGWP and finds a TEER 1 data role. After completing 1,560 eligible work hours and meeting the language requirement, the graduate may qualify for CEC.

Another master’s student may already have several years of skilled foreign experience and become eligible through FSWP earlier.

The master’s degree creates time and education points. Your work, language result and overall profile create the actual PR pathway.

Canada PR Requirements for International Students

Canada PR requirements for international students depend on the chosen pathway, but most graduates should prepare these core elements:

Requirement

What to check

Your studies and employment must be authorised

Eligible work experience

Confirm the duration, location and TEER

Correct NOC

Match your duties rather than the job title

Approved language test

Competitive CRS score

Eligibility does not guarantee an invitation

Education evidence

Keep transcripts and completion documents

Employment evidence

Record duties, salary, hours and dates

Admissibility

Police and medical checks may apply

Proof of funds

Required for certain pathways

Provincial connection

Required for relevant PNP streams

Express Entry accepts IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General and PTE Core for English. It accepts TEF Canada and TCF Canada for French.

IELTS Academic is not accepted for Express Entry.

Language results must remain valid when you create your profile and when you submit your permanent residence application.

Applicants with a break in education should also understand how a Canadian study gap may be assessed. A logical study plan matters before the post-study work stage begins.

How Long Does It Take to Get PR in Canada After Study?

There is no single Canada PR processing time after study because the journey contains separate stages.

Stage

Practical timeframe

Canadian study

Eight months to four years or more

Eligible CEC work

At least 12 months

Waiting for an invitation

Depends on CRS score and invitation rounds

PR application processing

Depends on the programme and current caseload

A student completing a two-year diploma may need around three years simply to finish the study and CEC work stages.

Government PR processing begins only after the applicant becomes eligible, receives an invitation and submits a complete application.

Use the official application processing-time checker instead of relying on an estimate copied from an older article.

Canada PR Fees and Proof of Funds

Item

Current amount

Economic PR application for one adult

CAD 1,590

PGWP government fees

CAD 255

Settlement funds for one person, where required

CAD 15,263

CEC applicants do not normally need settlement funds.

Applicants under the Federal Skilled Worker Program and Federal Skilled Trades Program generally need to show settlement funds unless the relevant exemption applies.

IRCC updates financial requirements periodically. Check the official proof-of-funds table before submitting your profile.

Documents Needed for PR After Study

Prepare these documents before your work permit begins to run short:

  • passport;
  • Canadian transcript and completion letter;
  • PGWP and previous status documents;
  • approved language result;
  • employment reference letter;
  • payslips and tax records;
  • police certificates;
  • medical examination, when requested;
  • proof of funds, if required;
  • Educational Credential Assessment;
  • provincial nomination, if applicable;
  • marriage and dependent documents, if applicable.

Your employment reference letter should show your duties, salary, weekly hours, employment dates and employer contact details.

A letter that only confirms your title may not prove that the work matches the NOC you selected.

Common Mistakes That Reduce PR Chances

Common mistakes include:

  • choosing a programme without checking PGWP eligibility;
  • assuming every DLI programme qualifies for a PGWP;
  • ignoring the programme’s CIP code;
  • counting full-time student work towards CEC;
  • selecting a NOC from the job title alone;
  • taking the wrong language test;
  • allowing a passport expiry to shorten the PGWP;
  • waiting until the PGWP is close to expiry before checking CRS;
  • submitting an incomplete employment reference;
  • choosing a province only because somebody calls it easy.

Frequently Asked Questions

How to get PR in Canada after study?

Complete a PGWP-eligible Canadian programme, obtain a PGWP where possible, gain qualifying work experience, take an approved language test and apply through CEC, FSWP, PNP or another suitable pathway.

Can I apply for PR while studying in Canada?

Can I get PR after a one-year course in Canada?

Yes, but the route can be risky because a one-year non-master’s programme may lead to a short PGWP. Previous foreign experience or a provincial pathway may become important.

Can I get PR after a two-year diploma?

Yes. An eligible two-year programme may lead to a PGWP of up to three years, giving you more time to obtain qualifying employment. PR is still not automatic.

Can I get PR in Canada after a master’s degree?

Yes. An eligible master’s programme of at least eight months may lead to a three-year PGWP. You must still qualify through CEC, FSWP, PNP or another pathway.

How long does it take to get PR after study in Canada?

Many students need several years when study duration and the time required to gain skilled work are included. The exact period depends on your pathway, CRS score, invitation timing and IRCC processing.

Final Study-to-PR Checklist

Before choosing or completing your programme:

  1. Confirm that the programme is PGWP eligible.
  2. Check whether a field-of-study requirement applies.
  3. Estimate the likely PGWP duration.
  4. Identify the NOC and TEER of your target job.
  5. Compare CEC, FSWP, PNP and regional pathways.
  6. Take the correct language test early.
  7. Calculate your CRS score.
  8. Keep evidence for every month of qualifying work.

Study creates the opportunity. Eligible work, language ability and the right pathway turn that opportunity into a credible permanent residence plan.
